title: Manifest-driven unmarshalers for streamed structured responses
creator: Evan Zhao
description: Implement a manifest-driven unmarshaller system for the Go SDK that lets callers declare typed struct shapes and per-field decoders via a small manifest DSL. The goal is to make decoding structured outputs from streamed responses ergonomic, memory-safe, and composable with the SDK's retry and streaming backpressure semantics. This RFC+implementation pairs a tiny manifest format with a set of generic helpers so consumers can: 1) incrementally decode out-of-band JSON chunks, 2) map envelopes to typed structs without intermediate allocations, 3) attach per-field validators and transformers, and 4) plug decoding behavior into the streaming iterator and retry middleware.
acceptance_criteria: Library exposes a Manifest type that maps field keys to typed decoder functions (using generics) and can be instantiated with struct tags or builder helpers
Stream iterator can incrementally apply the manifest to each partial payload chunk and yield typed values without buffering the entire response
Decoders support small-state accumulation (e.g., collecting tokens for a nested object) and explicit cancellation when retry/backoff triggers a non-retryable error
Examples and smoke tests show integration with SDK retry middleware: when transient errors occur mid-stream, retried requests resume in a deterministic manner or surface a clear partial-result error
Benchmarks demonstrate no >10% regression in p50 token latency vs. the current unstructured decoder and reduced peak allocations for common shapes
Documentation and at least two example apps (chat with structured actions; long-form generation with clause annotations) included in repo/examples
tasks: Design: finalize manifest DSL and API surface (prototype types, builder, tag mapping)
Implement core Manifest and generic Decoder interfaces with minimal runtime reflection
Integrate with stream iterator: hook decoders into chunk pipeline and add backpressure-aware flow control
Add retry-safety: define retry points, idempotency for partial decode, and graceful abort behavior
Write unit tests for nested objects, arrays, optional fields, and error propagation
Create performance microbenchmarks comparing allocations and throughput vs. current decoder
Author examples: example-chat-structured-actions and clause-annotator, add README and usage snippets
Code review, iterate on feedback, merge, and cut release branch for go-sdk-0.18
comments: 2025-02-12 - Evan Zhao: initial spike shows manifest builder can be implemented with two tiny generic interfaces; reflection minimized by code generation fallback for unusual shapes
2025-02-18 - Priya Desai: design review notes - prefer explicit decoder registration over implicit struct tags for clearer error messages in streaming contexts
2025-02-21 - Miguel Santos: prototype memory pool reduced allocations by ~35% in parse-heavy test; need to ensure pools are goroutine-safe
2025-02-26 - Design review (Leah O'Connor): examples should surface structured action schemas used by the Console; add one example that emits rollout decisions

2025-02-28 - Engineering: discovered an edge-case where partial JSON objects split across chunks produce ambiguous token boundaries; resolved by adding a bounded reassembly buffer with configurable size
notes: Decision: use a tiny manifest DSL that can be auto-generated from struct tags but is first-class as code to avoid reflection at runtime
Trade-off: bounded reassembly buffer simplifies token boundary handling but requires tuning for very large embedded blobs; default to 16KB with override

Retry semantics: for non-idempotent streams (append-only) we will return a partial-result error with explicit checkpoint token; for idempotent responses we will attempt a resumed request when the upstream API supports range/resume
Ergonomics: provide a small set of generic decoder helpers (StringField[T], IntField[T], Nested[T]) and a Compose helper for commonly used transformations
Testing: add fuzz tests to validate decoder behavior for chunk splits, escaped characters, and non-UTF8 bytes
Docs: include a migration guide from unstructured json.RawMessage-based handlers to manifest-driven decoders
